Nessa asked whether she can do three runs next week plus the two she missed. The draft answers that clearly: no, missed runs can't be made up, and five runs straight after a fever invites a setback. The week opens with a full rest day and a gentle walk. It cuts to two short, easy walk-runs on her usual days, so volume drops well below her 6.8 to 7.3 km weeks. That covers rest for illness (check 5) and backing off for exhaustion (check 8), and nothing jumps. There's a safety flag to get the fever and cough seen if they don't settle, and each day is specific enough to run as written.

Why not a 5: she's still coughing, blocked up and "wiped out." Neither run comes with a condition such as skip it if the cough or tiredness isn't easing, or if the fever comes back. The referral is vague too ("if they do not settle"). Saturday also jumps from 1-minute to 2-minute run intervals within the first week back. That isn't unsafe, but it's a bit brisk. The draft also never mentions the 15 November race, so she doesn't hear how this week fits her goal.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: This is a restart week, not a catch-up week. …
Answers: (1) No. Don't add the two missed runs, and don't go back to three runs yet. (2) A missed run can't be banked, and squeezing five runs into a week when you have just had a fever is the quickest way to a setback. …
Safety flag: Get the fever and cough checked if they do not settle
Next week:
Mon: rest. No running, and keep the dog walks short and gentle. You only cleared the…
Tue: other, 20 min easy walk, flat route, a pace where you can talk in full sentences…
Wed: easy, 20 min walk-run, 5 min walk then 5 x (1 min run, 2 min walk), effort 4 to 5…
Thu: rest. Dog walk only. Rest lets you absorb the first run back.
Fri: rest. Dog walk only. Another day to recover before Saturday's run.
Sat: easy, 24 min walk-run, 3 min walk then 7 x (2 min run, 1 min walk), effort 4 to 5…
Sun: rest. Dog walk only. Keeps the week light so next week can return to three runs.
